persona.name: Yui Takahara

occupation.title: Customer Success Specialist
occupation.organization: A 60-person HR-tech SaaS startup in Shibuya, Tokyo
occupation.description: Onboards mid-market clients onto the company's attendance management product, running 4-6 client calls a day plus internal standups. Already runs a free-tier AI notetaker on every call and pastes the summaries into Notion. Has zero purchasing authority but her tool experiments have a way of spreading through the company Slack.

persona.education: Sociology degree from Waseda University; first job at a mobile carrier shop counter, self-taught her way into SaaS.
long_term_goals: Move into a CS ops role designing processes rather than running calls
Speak at a SaaS community meetup
Save enough to stop worrying about Tokyo rent
Take a working-holiday style month in Fukuoka or Taipei
persona.style: Fast, upbeat talker who punctuates sentences with 'nanka' and laughs easily, though she tightens up around executives. Narrates her workflow enthusiastically and screenshots everything — her explanations come with images before words. Chronically overcommits, then apologizes with sticker-laden Slack messages at midnight.

traits: Early adopter who churns through tools monthly
Optimistic to a fault about new tech
Slightly disorganized despite loving productivity apps

interests: Notion templates and CS ops workflows
likes: Free tiers she can trial without asking anyone
Sharing 'this changed my life' tool finds
dislikes: Writing minutes by hand after a call
Approval processes that take three weeks
Being told 'we've always done it this way'

beliefs: If a tool saves ten minutes a day it pays for itself
The person closest to the work should pick the tools
AI summaries are drafts, not gospel — you still skim the recording
skills: Turning messy call notes into follow-up emails fast
Reading a customer's mood on video calls

general: Records every client call with consent and lets the AI notetaker summarize
Trials a new productivity app roughly every month
Evangelizes tools in the #tool-jiman Slack channel
Forgets to expense things until finance chases her

morning: 8:00 wake, convenience store coffee on the walk to the station
Checks overnight client tickets on the Hibiya line
workday: Evening: cleans AI summaries into Notion and sends follow-ups
evening: Gym twice a week or drinks with coworkers
YouTube and tool-Twitter scrolling before bed
weekend: Saturday cafe + side-learning (SQL course, currently stalled)
Sunday K-pop content and meal-prep attempts

health.physical: Healthy; mild eye strain and shoulder stiffness from six hours of daily video calls.
health.mental: Generally buoyant, with periodic overwhelm spikes when client renewals cluster.

relationships.name: Haruka
relationships.description: A nurse who teases Yui for automating everything but still can't split the utility bills without her.

relationships.name: Kudo-san
relationships.description: Supportive but budget-less; tells her 'write it up and I'll raise it at the leaders meeting' about every tool she proposes.
